sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Glynn County?
sections.html:
The Glynn County Tax Commissioner bills and collects property tax, and the Property Appraisal Office values the land and buildings. The tax office is at 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, in Brunswick, and its phone is 912-554-7000. Counter hours there run 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays. Valuation questions go to the appraisal office, Suite 101 at the same address, 912-554-7093, which keeps 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM hours.

The tax commissioner's page describes the office as responsible for billing, collecting and distributing ad valorem and title ad valorem taxes, running delinquent tax sales and preparing the annual digest. A seller with a question about a balance, a split bill or a lien should call the tax office first and the appraisal office for anything about value.

sections.h2: Where does a Glynn County house sit on the map and in the market?
sections.html:
Glynn County sits on the southeast Georgia coast, with Brunswick as the county seat. It was one of Georgia's original eight counties, created on February 5, 1777, and it includes the Sea Islands of Jekyll Island, St. Simons Island and Sea Island. Wikipedia lists a total area of 585 square miles, of which about 28 percent is water, and Interstate 95 and US 17 are among its main routes.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table estimates the county at 87,599 people in July 2025, a gain of 3.7 percent since the 2020 census count. It reports 45,747 housing units, a 66.7 percent owner-occupied rate, and a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied value of $301,300. Median household income is $69,799 and the mean commute is 20.0 minutes. Building permits numbered 448 in 2025.

Brunswick is the only incorporated city listed on the county's Wikipedia page, so most island and mainland addresses are unincorporated and are billed through the county. Ask the tax commissioner whether a particular parcel carries any additional district charge.

sections.h2: When are Glynn County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Glynn bills real estate and personal property once a year, usually in September, with payment due in November. For 2026 the bills were mailed on September 17, went online on September 18, and carried a due date of November 17, 2026. The county's pay page notes that billing and due dates can change depending on the state's acceptance of the digest.

The Property Appraisal Office posts a yearly calendar. The dates below come from that page and the tax commissioner's payment page.

Glynn County yearly property tax calendar

Source: Glynn County Property Appraisal Office, Important Dates, and Glynn County Tax Commissioner, Pay/View Tax Bills.

sections.h2: What happens when a Glynn County tax bill is paid late?
sections.html:
Late payment adds interest, a penalty and, eventually, levy fees. The county's pay page says interest is calculated monthly starting the day after the due date and is set at the federal level. A 5 percent penalty applies to the past due principal every 120 days, up to 20 percent of the bill. Fees begin once the levy process starts and keep growing on a schedule until the day of a sale.

The office then follows a written sequence under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3:

  • After the last day for payment, the tax commissioner sends a written notice that the taxes are outstanding.
  • If nothing is paid within 30 days, an execution (called a Fi.Fa.) is issued against the owner and the property, with a $13.00 issuance fee.
  • The execution is recorded in the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Payments go to the oldest year owed first, and partial payments can be made online only.

An owner who is behind and wants to sell should ask the tax office for a payoff figure before listing, because a recorded execution has to be cleared at closing.

sections.h2: How do Glynn County homestead exemptions and appeals work?
sections.html:
The deadline to file for homestead exemption in Glynn County is April 1. Georgia's Department of Revenue explains that an application may be made at any time after the home becomes the primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought, and that failing to apply is treated as a waiver. Ask the appraisal office which local exemptions apply to your address and what proof it wants.

To challenge a value, use the annual assessment notice. State guidance says the appeal must be sent to the board of tax assessors and postmarked no later than 45 days from the mailing date of the notice. The county calendar places that window in June and July, and the exact last day is printed on your notice.

A refund claim for taxes erroneously or illegally assessed must be started within three years of payment, per the state's county property tax facts page.

sections.h2: How are Glynn County tax payments made and billed to a new owner?
sections.html:
Payments can be made online, by mail, in the office or through drop boxes at the front and back of the Harold Pate building. Online card payments carry a service fee of 2.95 percent with a $2.50 minimum, and electronic checks cost $1.50. The county says it does not collect or keep any of those fees. Checks go to Glynn County Tax Commissioner, 1725 Reynolds Street, Suite 100, Brunswick, GA 31520, with the parcel or bill number, property address and a phone number written on them.

State law sends the bill to the person who owned the property on January 1. The county mails a separate new owner bill at the same time or near the end of the year, and the tax liability stays with the new or current owner. Your contract decides who repays whom. The office also does not mail bills to mortgage companies, so a borrower with escrow should confirm that the servicer received the bill.

sections.h2: How does a Glynn County house sale handle tax at closing?
sections.html:
The closing attorney asks the tax commissioner for the current balance, and any open amount is paid from the seller's proceeds. Georgia's tax year follows the January 1 owner, so a mid-year sale usually needs a proration written into the contract. Ask the tax office whether a bill has been issued yet for the year you are selling in.

We buy Glynn County houses as-is, including homes on Brunswick streets and mainland lots with a delinquent balance or a recorded execution. A cash purchase still goes through a title search, and the tax payoff is handled the same way. If you inherited a coastal house that needs repairs, tell us the parcel number and we will look at it. For a property owned through a transfer on death deed, see our Georgia guide on that deed.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 due date for Glynn County property tax?
faqs.a: November 17, 2026. The county mailed bills on September 17 and posted them online on September 18, 2026.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal a Glynn County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is 45 days after the mailing date printed on your annual assessment notice. The county calendar shows these notices going out in May and June, with appeals in June and July.

faqs.q: Will the lender on my Glynn County home receive the tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The tax commissioner says it does not send bills directly to mortgage companies. If your lender pays through escrow, confirm with the servicer that the bill was received.

faqs.q: Are installment payments allowed on Glynn County property tax?
faqs.a: Partial payments are available online only. Georgia does not allow increment payments on current year taxes until the digest has been accepted and a bill is produced.

faqs.q: What does a late Glynn County tax payment cost?
faqs.a: The county lists monthly interest plus a 5 percent penalty on the past due principal every 120 days, capped at 20 percent. Levy fees add on once the process begins.
